title: bug: account rotation relaunches an interactive claude seat on an account that never accepted folder trust, so the TUI silently blocks at the trust dialog
description:
Observed 2026-10-25 by governor-187cc44e.

At 10:58:51Z interactive architect-26ba32c3 rotated from acct-2 to acct-4 (wrapper_restart). The wrapper's pre-flight then claimed task-5c71dff9 and preloaded its context (worker status READING_CONTEXT).

The claude TUI, pid 1795029 with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=acct-4, never produced a transcript. No acct-*/projects/*/*.jsonl contains its pre-flight prompt, and it made no moe tool call afterwards. The heartbeat sidecar kept lastActivityAt fresh, so for 40+ minutes it looked alive while the board's planning queue grew to about 12 rows.

Reading each account's .claude.json, projects['/mnt/d/projexts/moes'].hasTrustDialogAccepted is:
- true for acct-1, acct-2 and acct-5
- missing for acct-3, acct-4 and acct-6

Those three only ever ran headless -p seats for moes, and -p skips the trust dialog. An interactive launch on them therefore stops at "Do you trust the files in this folder?" until a human answers, invisible to the daemon and the governor.

Expected: an interactive claude seat never parks silently on a first-run dialog after rotation. Possible fixes, for the planner to choose:
- the accounts add/login flow pre-accepts trust for the projects it serves;
- the lease steers interactive seats to accounts that already trust the project;
- the wrapper detects the condition and refuses with a named code and a #general escalation, instead of launching into a dialog.

Note the rotation invariant in scripts/CLAUDE.md: "The wrapper never opens a file inside a config directory". A fix that touches .claude.json must either respect that invariant or get human sign-off to amend it. Both launchers must stay at parity.
definitionOfDone: An interactive claude seat that the rotation moves to an account without folder trust for the project either launches without stopping at the trust dialog, or is refused before launch with a named code and a #general escalation that names the account and the project. It never parks silently.
Headless -p seats are unchanged, and the scripts/CLAUDE.md rotation invariant is either preserved or explicitly amended with human sign-off.

The sh and ps1 launchers behave identically, and bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh passes. Regression coverage in scripts/tests/moe-account-lease.test.mjs or [accounts] postflight cases exercises the untrusted-account path. Any daemon change passes cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test.
docs/MCP_SERVER.md 'Claude Account Rotation' and scripts/CLAUDE.md describe the behavior.

implementationPlan.description:
Helper `trust` subcommand, test-first (load test-driven-development). Facts measured by the architect 2026-10-26 (claude 2.1.310 + the live account configs; keys/booleans only were read): claude's trust check reads projects[<git toplevel of the cwd, else the cwd>] in $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.claude.json, then walks from the cwd up to the repo root; accepting the dialog writes that same key, '/' separators on Windows (live keys: WSL '/mnt/d/projexts/moes', native 'D:/projexts/moes'); claude saves the file under a proper-lockfile mkdir lock at `<file>.lock`, re-reading under it, as JSON.stringify(cfg, null, 2) with no trailing newline.

scripts/moe-account-lease.mjs: add `trust <configDir> <projectDir> [<launchDir>]` (launchDir defaults to projectDir; ps1 passes claude's real launch cwd). It prints exactly one line, exit 0:
- `trusted` (every key already trusted; nothing written)
- `granted` (missing keys written and read back)
- `refused<TAB><sec><TAB><reason>`: sec = MOE_ACCOUNT_RETRY_SEC as an integer >= 1, else 300 (pick's cap rule); reason is one of, verbatim: 'no .claude.json in the account folder' | "the account's .claude.json is not a regular file" | "the account's .claude.json is over 16 MiB" | "the account's .claude.json is not a JSON object" | "the account's .claude.json is locked by another claude" | "the account's .claude.json could not be rewritten" | 'the trust entry did not read back' | 'the launch directory is outside the project'.
Missing args: exit 2 with USAGE (add `trust` to it and to the header list).

Export for tests: `trustKeys(dir, { platform, realpath, gitTop })` = deduped keys from dir, realpath(dir) and gitTop(dir) (`git -C <dir> rev-parse --show-toplevel`, 10s timeout, windowsHide, skipped on failure). win32: path.win32.resolve, '\\' -> '/', strip a trailing '/' (keep 'X:/'), plus the same key with an uppercased drive letter. posix: path.posix.resolve, strip trailing '/'. Also export the IO function with an injectable lock wait (default 2000 ms).

Algorithm:
1. launchDir must be projectDir or inside it (win32: compare the normalized forms case-insensitively). Else print `trusted` when every launchDir key is already trusted, otherwise the 'outside' refusal.
2. Unlocked fast path: lstat <configDir>/.claude.json (missing / symlink / not a file -> refused); size <= 16 MiB; JSON.parse to a plain object whose `projects` is absent or a plain object. If every key has hasTrustDialogAccepted === true -> `trusted`.
3. Else take claude's own lock: fs.mkdirSync(<configDir>/.claude.json.lock), retry every 50 ms until the wait ends (Atomics.wait sleep). Never remove a lock this call did not create; release ours in finally.
4. Re-read under the lock with the same checks. Set each missing key: projects[k] = {...existing object entry or {}, hasTrustDialogAccepted: true} (the minimal entry claude's runner writes). Every other key is untouched.
5. Write JSON.stringify(next, null, 2) (no trailing newline) to <configDir>/.claude.json.moe-<pid>.tmp with the original mode, then renameSync over the file, retrying EPERM/EBUSY/EACCES 5x50 ms (Windows). Unlink the tmp on failure.
6. Re-read and verify every key -> `granted`.

Error handling: every fs/git failure maps to one fixed reason. Nothing from the file, no path and no env value is ever printed; no exception escapes main. Rewrite the header comment: the helper opens exactly one file inside a config folder, .claude.json, only to set this trust key for an interactive seat (human sign-off 2026-10-26, task-7a0b1881); it never opens .credentials.json or any other file.

Tests in scripts/tests/moe-account-lease.test.mjs (node:test, temp dirs only, never a real account folder):
(a) trustKeys:
- posix: given + realpath + gitTop, deduped, trailing slash stripped;
- win32: 'D:\\projexts\\moes\\' -> 'D:/projexts/moes';
- win32: 'd:\\x' also yields 'D:/x'.
(b) Untrusted config -> `granted`:
- every key now trusted;
- every other top-level key and project entry deep-equals the seed;
- an existing entry keeps its fields;
- 2-space JSON, no trailing newline;
- POSIX mode preserved;
- no .lock dir or *.tmp left.
(c) Already trusted -> `trusted`; bytes and mtimeMs unchanged.
(d) Missing file -> refused; nothing is created.
(e) Malformed JSON / an array / a non-object `projects` -> refused; bytes unchanged.
(f) A file over 16 MiB -> refused.
(g) A symlinked .claude.json -> the regular-file refusal, and the link stays. Use the canSymlink guard from mem:decision-posix-only-test-guards.
(h) A pre-existing .claude.json.lock dir -> the locked refusal within the injected wait; the foreign lock is not removed and the file is unchanged.
(i) launchDir outside projectDir -> 'outside'; launchDir inside -> granted.
(j) CLI:
- exactly one stdout line;
- with MOE_ACCOUNT_RETRY_SEC=7 the line is `refused\t7\t...`;
- a secret marker seeded in the config never appears on stdout or stderr;
- missing args -> exit 2.
Red first: the run must fail on the missing export or subcommand.
implementationPlan.note:
Added the helper's `trust <configDir> <projectDir> [<launchDir>]` subcommand. It prints exactly one line: trusted | granted | refused<TAB><sec><TAB><reason>, using the 8 verbatim reasons. Missing args exit 2 with USAGE.

Exports:
- trustKeys(dir, {platform, realpath, gitTop})
- launchInside(projectDir, launchDir, platform), exported so the win32 case-insensitive check can be tested
- trustLine(configDir, projectDir, launchDir, {env, lockWaitMs, platform, realpath, gitTop})

Write path: an unlocked fast path, then claude's mkdir lock `.claude.json.lock` (50 ms polls, 2 s default wait). It re-reads under the lock, sets the missing keys only, writes a tmp file in the same folder (flag wx, chmod to the original mode), renames with 5x50 ms retries on EPERM/EBUSY/EACCES, reads back, and releases only its own lock in `finally`. retryCapSec() is now shared with pickLine (same cap rule). The header comment was rewritten for the one-file exception, citing the sign-off.

Tests: 13 new (a-j plus a read-only-folder case and a 16 MiB boundary). RED first: the import failed on the missing launchInside export. Now `node --test scripts/tests/moe-account-lease.test.mjs` gives 31 tests, 30 pass, 0 fail, 1 skip (the existing Windows-only cmd case).

Mutation probes on a temp copy all fail at least 1 test (15 mutations): drop chmod, size `>`→`>=`, every→some, removing a foreign lock, the `..` check, the outside-already-trusted branch, overwriting the entry, a trailing newline, the uppercase drive, the fast path, the lock release, the notFile check, the projects-type check, and retry cap `>=1`→`>=0`.

The file is 536 lines; it was already 341, over the 300 soft cap, and the plan puts trust here.

implementationPlan.description:
Bash wiring in scripts/moe-agent.sh get_account_lease, in the `leased` branch after the existing MOE_ACCOUNT_LEASED line. Only when $CLAUDE_INTERACTIVE = true (headless -p seats never run it): trust=$("$NODE_CMD" "$ACCOUNT_HELPER" trust "$f3" "$PROJECT" 2>/dev/null) || trust="". claude runs after `cd "$PROJECT"`, so the launch dir is the project.

On its answer:
- `trusted`: return 0.
- `granted`: account_say "MOE_ACCOUNT_TRUST_GRANTED account=$f1 project=$PROJECT" "$GREEN"; return 0.
- `refused<TAB>sec<TAB>reason`:
  - clear_account_lease.
  - account_say "MOE_ACCOUNT_UNTRUSTED account=$f1 project=$PROJECT ($reason) - not launching into Claude's folder-trust dialog; retry in ${sec}s, the held task stays held. (Ctrl+C to stop)".
  - Post ONE #general escalation per get_account_lease call per account (keep a local list of ids already escalated). Follow the announce_push_failure pattern: moe_rpc chat_send, JSON args built with $PYTHON_CMD, best-effort. Text: "@governors $WORKER_ID: MOE_ACCOUNT_UNTRUSTED - account $f1 does not trust project $PROJECT and Moe could not grant it ($reason). The interactive seat waits instead of parking at Claude's folder-trust dialog. Fix: start claude once in $PROJECT under that account's folder (claude-accounts/$f1) and accept the trust dialog." Never include the config directory path: the [accounts] harness forbids any account directory reaching the daemon.
  - sleep "$sec"; continue (re-lease; the daemon may hand out another account).
- Anything else (empty output, a helper crash): clear_account_lease plus the existing 'MOE_ACCOUNT_LEASE_UNAVAILABLE (the account helper failed) - launching without rotation.'; return 0. This keeps the existing every-failure-launches-unrotated rule.

Amend the block comment (~line 5950) and the call-site comment (~line 7278): nothing reads inside an account folder except an interactive seat's trust key.

scripts/tests/postflight.sh [accounts]:
- After the five headless runs, assert $ACCT_HOME/acct-1 and acct-2 are still empty (headless seats never touch a config folder).
- Before `run_accounts interactive`, seed $ACCT_HOME/acct-1/.claude.json with an untrusted config: an unrelated trusted project, an oauthAccount carrying a secret marker, and other keys. This is REQUIRED: without it the existing interactive run now refuses and waits until its timeout.

  - the projects entry whose key realpath-equals PROJECT_DIR has hasTrustDialogAccepted true (compare by realpath: under Git Bash, MSYS converts "$PROJECT" for node.exe, so the key is the Windows form);
  - every other seeded key deep-equals the seed;
  - no .claude.json.lock or *.tmp left in acct-1;
  - the marker appears nowhere in the wrapper output or the RPC log;

implementationPlan.description:
PowerShell twin in scripts/moe-agent.ps1 Get-MoeAccountLease, in the `leased` branch. The file is UTF-8 WITH a BOM and LF line endings; keep both. Use PowerShell 5.1 syntax only (no ??, no ternary, no &&).

Only when $claudeInteractive: run Invoke-MoeAccountHelper -HelperArgs @('trust', $f[3], $projectPath, (Get-Location).ProviderPath). A ps1 claude launch runs in the launcher's cwd (root CLAUDE.md), and the JetBrains plugin opens that terminal in project.basePath.

On its answer:
- `trusted`: return.
- `granted`: green Write-Host of the same '[account] MOE_ACCOUNT_TRUST_GRANTED account=... project=<$projectPath>' line.
- `refused`:
  - Clear-MoeAccountLease.
  - The same yellow MOE_ACCOUNT_UNTRUSTED line, byte-identical to sh apart from variable syntax.
  - The same escalation via Send-MoeGeneralChat, once per call per account.
  - Start-Sleep -Seconds <sec>; continue.
- $null or unknown output: Clear-MoeAccountLease plus the existing MOE_ACCOUNT_LEASE_UNAVAILABLE line; return.

Amend the block comment (~line 5398) and the call-site comment (~line 6434) like the sh twin.

parity-check compares the MOE_ACCOUNT_* code sets, so both files must carry MOE_ACCOUNT_TRUST_GRANTED and MOE_ACCOUNT_UNTRUSTED. The ps1 cases from step 2 are verified natively in step 6.
implementationPlan.note:
moe-agent.ps1 Get-MoeAccountLease is the twin of the sh step. When $claudeInteractive, after MOE_ACCOUNT_LEASED, it runs Invoke-MoeAccountHelper @('trust', $f[3], $projectPath, (Get-Location).ProviderPath). Its answers:
- trusted: return.
- granted: the green TRUST_GRANTED line.
- refused (split on tab, at least 3 fields): Clear-MoeAccountLease, the yellow UNTRUSTED line (byte-identical to sh apart from variable syntax), then Send-MoeGeneralChat once per account per call. The once-per-account record is an ordinal HashSet[string], so account ids stay case-sensitive. Then Start-Sleep and continue.
- $null or anything else: Clear-MoeAccountLease plus the existing LEASE_UNAVAILABLE line, return.

Code details:
- The escalation text uses ${WorkerId}: because `$WorkerId:` would not parse.
- The block comment, the call-site comment and the "free or trusted account" launch-time comment are amended.
- Encoding is preserved: BOM ef bb bf, 0 CR.
- PS 5.1 syntax only: no ??, &&, or ternary in the added lines.

implementationPlan.description:
Adversarial self-review of the whole diff (load adversarial-self-review). Check:
- Lock: no path deletes a lock this call did not create; finally always releases ours; a kill while holding it is recovered by claude's 10s stale rule.
- Atomicity: tmp and rename in the same folder; the tmp is cleaned on every failure; the file mode is preserved.
- Content: no line can print .claude.json content, a path from it, or an env value; the escalation never carries the config dir.
- Scope: only interactive leased claude seats; headless and unrotated launches behave exactly as before; only the trust key changes, and every other key round-trips.
- Keys: correct for WSL/Linux, native (D:/...), Git Bash (MSYS-converted args), a project nested in a git repo (the toplevel key is what claude's dialog writes), and trailing slashes.
- Loop: a refusal clears the lease, waits once per iteration, escalates once per account per call, and Ctrl+C still ends it; a helper crash launches unrotated.

Fix any finding, then rerun step 6 before moe.complete_task.

I ran the adversarial self-review over git diff of the 7 owned paths. Fixes from it: the three pre-gate fixes already listed in step 6 (fast-path parse failure re-read under the lock; trusted vs granted on the locked re-read; git run from node's own folder, not the project cwd, plus a test). Step 6 was rerun after them and is green.

Checklist results:
- Lock: only grantLocked's finally removes a lock, and only one its own mkdir created. A foreign lock is waited on (2 s) and then refused as "locked", never removed (test).
- Atomicity: the tmp file sits in the same folder, uses flag wx, and its mode is chmod'ed to the original. The rename retries 5x50 ms on EPERM/EBUSY/EACCES. The tmp is removed on every failure path.
- Content: nothing prints .claude.json content (a secret-marker CLI test and the postflight ACCT_SECRET check). The escalation is the plan's verbatim text: account id, project and fixed reason, never $f3. The claude-accounts/<id> hint is the plan's wording, not the leased directory.
- Scope: only interactive leased claude seats run the trust step. Headless output is byte-identical (lease-loop test, and postflight checks the account folders stay empty after the 5 -p runs). Every other key round-trips: postflight deep-equals against the seed, and a unit test checks key order.
- Keys: WSL/Linux posix paths; Windows D:/ form plus an uppercase drive; the real path; the git top-level; a trailing slash is trimmed. A project nested in a larger repo also trusts the repo top-level. That is the same key claude's own dialog writes, so it widens nothing beyond what a human Accept writes.
- Loop: a refusal clears the lease, sleeps once per iteration, and escalates once per account per get_account_lease call (dedup test). Ctrl+C ends it the same way as the existing MOE_ACCOUNT_WAIT sleep. A helper crash or garbage reply launches unrotated with MOE_ACCOUNT_LEASE_UNAVAILABLE (test).
- Parity: identical codes and lines; parity-check sh+ps1 PASS. ps1 BOM kept, 0 CR, PS 5.1 parse 0 errors.
- No real account folder was touched: tests use temp dirs with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR stripped. No .claude.json.lock or .moe-*.tmp exists under ~/.moe/claude-accounts/*.

Residuals (theoretical, documented, not fixed):
1. A helper killed while holding the lock leaves it. Trust is then refused as "locked" until claude on that account clears it under its 10 s stale rule. This is loud, not silent.
2. A kill between the write and the rename leaves a harmless .claude.json.moe-<pid>.tmp.
3. Claude's own no-lock fallback write could race and drop the key. The next launch then re-grants it.
4. A ps1 launch from a cwd outside the project refuses loudly by design, unless that cwd is already trusted.
5. The daemon may re-lease the same untrusted account. The seat then waits MOE_ACCOUNT_RETRY_SEC per round, with one escalation per call.
6. MOE_ACCOUNT_RETRY_SEC above 2^31-1 parses differently in sh and ps1. This is the same pre-existing idiom as the MOE_ACCOUNT_WAIT branch; sh prints a "[: integer expression expected" line for values above int64 and falls back to 300.

claude internals (2.1.310):
- GP() trust = CLAUDE_CODE_SANDBOXED, or session trust, or projects[ZVe()] (the git root of the cwd), or a walk from the cwd up to the repo root.

- Format: 2-space JSON, no trailing newline, mode 0600.

Wrapper structure:
- sh get_account_lease (~5984) and ps1 Get-MoeAccountLease (~5449) are twin loops (leased / wait / off / unavailable); the trust step slots into `leased`.
- Escalation patterns: sh announce_push_failure (moe_rpc chat_send + $PYTHON_CMD JSON); ps1 Send-MoeGeneralChat (~3954).

- Windows rename EPERM/EBUSY needs the retry.
- Claude internals may change between versions (key, lock path). Grant failures are loud, never silent; the documented key is Claude's own published remedy.

completionSummary:
An interactive claude seat that rotation moves onto an account without folder trust no longer parks silently at Claude's trust dialog.

How it works now:
- A new `trust` subcommand in scripts/moe-account-lease.mjs sets projects[<key>].hasTrustDialogAccepted in that account's .claude.json.
- Keys covered: the launch dir, its realpath and its git top-level, plus the Windows D:/ forms.
- The write happens under claude's own .claude.json.lock (mkdir, waits up to 2 s, never removes a foreign lock). It re-reads under the lock, uses tmp+rename with the original mode, and reads the file back. Every other key round-trips.
- Output is trusted | granted | refused\t<sec>\t<fixed reason>.

Wrapper behaviour (both launchers):
- sh get_account_lease and its ps1 twin Get-MoeAccountLease run the trust step for interactive leased claude seats only.
- granted prints MOE_ACCOUNT_TRUST_GRANTED.
- A refusal clears the lease and prints MOE_ACCOUNT_UNTRUSTED. It sends one #general @governors escalation per account per call, naming the account and project and never the config dir. It then waits MOE_ACCOUNT_RETRY_SEC and re-leases.
- A helper failure prints MOE_ACCOUNT_LEASE_UNAVAILABLE and launches unrotated.
- Headless -p seats are unchanged (byte-identical test, and postflight checks the account folders stay empty).

Sign-off: the invariant is amended with human sign-off (comment-99598cf0e7f64f2ca2db4a0886087a3e) in scripts/CLAUDE.md and docs/MCP_SERVER.md.

Tests:
- moe-account-lease.test.mjs: helper unit tests, plus real-function lease-loop tests on bash, powershell.exe, pwsh.exe and Git Bash.
- postflight [accounts]: the interactive run is seeded with a secret marker. It checks the grant, the deep-equal seed, and that the secret never appears. The cut-down RED run against the old wrapper fails with "expected MOE_ACCOUNT_TRUST_GRANTED".
